title: Control evidence
description: What the attest step recorded about each requirement: the result of each half of each control's paired proof, each setting read from the hosting platform, and each finding of the audit report. The file is written by `lisa controls attest` and is never edited by hand; `lisa controls attest --check` computes the verdict again from it and fails when the committed verdict differs.

schema_version.description: The version of this format. It changes only when a reader written for the previous version would misread the file.

records.description: One record per result per requirement, ordered by `id`. A result about a control that serves two requirements is two records.

criterion_id.description: A requirement id as the specification writes it, for example `AC5.4` or `SI7`.

utc_time.description: A time in UTC with milliseconds, `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ss.sssZ`.

record.description: One of three kinds of record, told apart by `rung`.

exercised_record.description: One half of a paired proof: a change was planted and the control's answer recorded.

command.description: What was started, one item per argument, or `null` when nothing was.

commit.description: The commit the repository's HEAD was at when the record was made, or `null` when the repository has no commit or is not a git repository.

completed_at.description: When its answer was in, in UTC. The freshness lifetime is counted from here.

criterion.description: The requirement the record is evidence for.

detail.description: The same as a sentence. On a `not-applicable` record it is the fact that makes the requirement not apply.

entry_id.description: The identifier of the register entry the record is about, for example `code-style@api`.

exit_status.description: The exit status of what was started, or `null` when nothing ran to an end.

freshness_seconds.description: How long after `completed_at` the record may be relied on, in whole seconds; never more than twelve months. Past that, the requirement reads `unknown`.

half.description: Which half: the change that breaks the rule, or the one that does not. Only an exercised record names a half.

id.description: The record's identifier, unique in the file. It is made only of what the record is about: `<entry id>/<moment>/<half or rung>/<requirement>` for a record about a control, `audit-finding/<requirement>@<folder>` for a record of an audit finding. No time and no counter goes into it, so the same proof of the same control has the same identifier on every run.

moment.description: The moment the record speaks for: `commit`, `push`, `pull-request`.

output_excerpt.description: The end of what the check printed; empty when nothing ran.

output_truncated.description: Whether the excerpt leaves out earlier output.

reason.description: A short, fixed word for why the record shows what it does: the proof's reason, or the audit finding's state.

result.description: `held`: the control did what the requirement asks. `failed`: it did not. `unknown`: there is no answer that can be relied on.

rung.description: A change was planted and the control's answer recorded.

scope.description: The folder the record is about, written from the repository root, or `.` for the whole repository.

started_at.description: When the record's check began, in UTC.

moment.description: Always `null`: an audit finding speaks for no moment.

reason.description: A short, fixed word for why the record shows what it does: the proof's reason, or the audit finding's state.

result.description: `held`: the audit found it written down or checked. `failed`: the audit found nothing that does it. `unknown`: the audit could not establish it. `not-applicable`: the requirement does not apply, and `detail` is the fact that makes it so.

rung.description: The audit read the repository and ran nothing, so its finding is said and not checked.

scope.description: The folder the record is about, written from the repository root, or `.` for the whole repository.

started_at.description: When the record's check began, in UTC.
